title: Instrument Tutorial: Cytek Aurora
text:
Changing Sheathe
Before starting, check the sheathe fluid container on the left side of the instrument. If it is running low, press the connector to dettach the fluidic line. Carefully carry the sheathe container to the sort room.
Touch the MilliQ station screen to waken the system (and if applicable close any pop-ups). On the outside of the sheathe container, each sharpie line denotes 1 liter. Designate the amount of liquid to dispense on the MilliQ screen.
Unscrew the lid, and leave it propped on the side. Proceed to start the MilliQ station and fill. Keep an eye on it just to ensure no issues are encountered. Once full, stop the MilliQ, tighten the lid, and then carry the bottle back to the Aurora. Proceed to reconnect the fluidic line.

title: Instrument Tutorial: Cytek Aurora
text:
Changing Waste
Due to our Enviromental Health and Safety (EHS) agreement, all waste needs to be resuspended in 10% bleach to ensure it is disinfected before it is flushed down the drain. Check to see the current level to determine whether you need to discard the waste before getting started. Generally, if there is more than 2 liters on the bottle (as designated by the sharpie marks), we recommend going ahead and emptying it.
Tap the lid twice to ensure any droplets in the cap drop down into the waste container. The waste container has a sensor line that is connected to the Cytek Aurora. It is important not to twist it (avoiding supercoils). Therefore, unscrew the lid by twisting the waste container to the left while holding the lid steady.
Once this is done, with both hands, carefully walk the waste tank to the sink. If you need assistance, grab the cart from the cell sorter room entryway and roll it to the sink.
Carefully, pour the waste down the sink, avoiding back-splashes to your arms, eyes or mouth. Once drained, turn on the faucet, and flush the sink with tap water for at least 30 seconds to avoid having bleach smell fill the entire hallway.
Carry the now empty waste container back to the bleach station under the LSR-II, placing it in the red secondary spill container to avoid bleach damaging the floors wax surface. Unscrew the household bleach cap, and pour up to the first red line on the outside of the waste container (roughly 3 glug sounds). Recap the bleach bottle.
Carefully return the waste with bleach to the Aurora, and screw back into place by twisting the container to the right while holding on to the cap.

title: Instrument Tutorial: Cytek Aurora
text:
Powering On
With the sheathe filled, and waste emptied, go ahead and power on the Cytek Aurora. This can be done by firmly pressing the power button that can be found on the upper left side of the instrument for a few seconds. You should hear the instrument power on and fans/cooling start up and remain on.
Proceed to waken the computer from sleep by clicking on the mouse or keyboard. In event it is off, press the computers power button and wait for the computer to boot and go through start-up.
All Cytek Auroras share the same password (see monitor screens white sticky note) for the computer login. After entering it, wait for Windows to complete logging in to avoid any computer stalls.
Double click on the SpectroFlo software icon, and wait for it to open. Proceed to login using your user account.

title: Instrument Tutorial: Cytek Aurora
text:
Instrument Start Up
Once the instrument is on, and software opened, the Cytek Aurora will undergo instrument startup. If no water 5 ml tube is placed on the sip, you will get a pop-up asking that you place one on the SIP. Once placed, you will see the SIP line drop down to the bottom of the tube a couple times, water will be uptaken, and internal resevoir flushed to waste tank. Once this process is complete, you will see the cytometer icon go from red, to yellow, to green.
At this point, the lasers are now on. However, we recommend waiting at least 15 minutes before running QC to allow them time to warm up and stabilize. This will ensure that when QC is run, it will be for the same conditions as when you are running samples, avoiding QC drifting mid-acquisition once the lasers have warmed up. Additionally, running QC too early can result in QC fail with innapropiate settings.
Since we are a shared resource facility, you are at the mercy of the last user. We consequently recommend running a Clean Flow Cell at startup to flush out the fluidic lines of any debris, remaining cells, etc. that the last user may have left. This can be done by opening the QC tab, and accessing the cytometer gear icon on the left-side of the screen. You can then select the Clean Flow Cell icon.
The pop-up will request a bleach and a water tube. Due to issues with bleach damaging the QC beads, we do not use bleach, but flush with contrad (a detergent) instead. Discard any old contrad, water, sample tubes on the rack, and prepare fresh contrad and water tube from the yellow and blue squeeze bottles next to the instrument. If these are low, borrow from the next instrument over. Fill only to half-the capacity of the 5 ml tubes (roughly the white holders on the rack) to avoid overflow when placed on the SIP.
Once the contrad and water tubes are prepared, place the contrad tube on the sip (pressing until you hear the click), and only then select Start on the pop-up. The instrument will start as soon as the button is clicked, regardless of the presence of a tube. It will proceed to rapidly flush the flow cell and fluidic lines with most of the contents of the tube. Once done, the sip line will withdraw from the tube and you will get a note asking you to switch in the water tube. Proceed to do so, and select start. It will then flush away any residual contrad from the lines.
At this point, generally still have 12 minutes for the instrument lasers to warm up. We will typically refill and then run the Contrad tube on High for 6 minutes, as it takes about that long to see events drop.
At this point, we will refill and run the Water tube for another 6 minutes, flushing the remaining contrad and cellular gunk that may have built up from the previous day.

title: Instrument Tutorial: Cytek Aurora
text:
Daily QC
The Cytek Auroras are able to adjust detector gains to account for instrumental changes, allowing the analyzers to perform consistently over long periods of time despite changes that occur as the lasers approach end-of-life, and detector arrays experience wear and tear. To do this, the instruments are calibrated using SpectroFlo QC Beads, which have a standardized brightness for each detector. During automated QC, the instrument will adjust the gains up and down to ensure the QC beads that are run match the designated target for the specific bead lots.
Our SpectroFlo QC beads are stored in the fridge of the Cell Sorter room. To access the room, grab the key from the desk drawer under our Flow Cytometry Altar. Once the door has been opened, prop it with the door stop, and return the key to the desk drawer.
The keys can be found in the large fridge next to the MilliQ station. They are located in the small Cytek box in the door. Please make sure you grab the SpectroFloQC bead vial with the check mark on it located on the left side of the box, and not the Cell Sorter Beads that are on the right side of the box (which will not work for QC setting).
Grab a clean 5 ml polystyrene tube from the clean tubes container on the table. Dispense roughly 300 ul of MilliQ water (1 cm) to the botton of the tube.
Vortex the SpectroFloQC beads vigorously for 30 seconds. Carefully dispense 1 drop into the tube (avoid coming in contact with the tube surface to avoid contamination). Cap the SpectroFloQC beads and return them to their box in the fridge, making sure the door is also closed properly. Unprop and lose the door to the cell sort room on your way out.
With a permanent marker, label your tube “SPFL” and the corresponding date. Vortex vigorously for 20 seconds. Open the QC tab in SpectroFlo, place the QC bead tube on the sip, and press start QC.
The instrument will then go through the automated QC process, you will see individual detectors appear and dissaper as different gains are attempted to get them to reach their respective targets. Once stability is reached, bead acquisition will start and you will see beads be acquired. At this point, the sip needle will withdraw from the tube, and you will be notified whether instrument has passed or failed QC.

title: Instrument Tutorial: Cytek Aurora
text:
Interpreting QC
If the instrument has passed QC, congratulations, you are now all set, and can proceed with your experiment setup and acquisition. if the QC has failed, you will need to decipher what is going on.
On Cytek Aurora instruments, a QC fail can be trigerred in two manners. Either the gain for a particular detector is double the original value compared to the installation value (typical of end-of-life lasers) or the % rCV value for FSC, SSC or the 3rd detector of each laser has exceeded 6 or 8 % (meaning increased spread). We track our instruments QC status on our website, where you can view the same data as shown on the instrument.
What to do in the event of a QC fail? First, note if it has also occured at another point this week. If it has, we are likely aware and are working to get a Cytek field-service-engineer out to make the repairs. If there has been no other fail, there are a couple possibilities. If the failure is because the instrument has not properly warmed up yet, running water for another 10 minutes will likely be sufficient. Alternatively, if the fail is due to debris build up on the flow cell, running contrad and water for another 10 minutes can be enough. Occasionally, if someone ran bleach despite warning, the QC beads can end up damaged, which in turn can affect the automated QC.
Scan the report and see if the result is due to gain changes or RCV (shown by red highlighting). If RCV, scan the column and see if multiple detectors are involved and are greater than 6%. If it is only one, or it is barely above the cutoff, you should be okay. If multiple, or values substantially greater, your data is likely to be affected. Reach out to staff if you have additional questions, or looking for advice.

title: UMGCCC FCSR
text:
Hi _______,
With the severe research restrictions in effect we just wanted to highlight a few areas to pay attention to when using the Aurora to keep it running properly:
MilliQ Water: The only water that should be used for the Aurora is from the MQ system that is located in the sorting room. The sorting room is locked so you will need the key that is found in the top drawer on the right side of Dr. Fan’s desk (The one with the giant wooden crate in front of it). The key will have a red string attached to it.
Startup: When the cytometer is initially booted up the reservoir tank may potentially overfill so please keep an eye on that, if it starts to over fill just turn off the cytometer and turn it back on. To see the reservoir tank, open the front of the instrument (lift top lid then open the front door). Once the water level stabilizes you can shut the front of the machine.
There can be a connection issue between the computer and cytometer when first connecting for the day. If you notice a red x icon next to “cytometer” on the bottom right hand of the screen shut down the SpectroFlo software and turn off the cytometer. I also make sure that the connector from the cytometer to the computer is secure (back right of cytometer). Turn everything back on and the cytometer will connect (you will know it’s working when portions of the cytometer start moving).
To warm up the lasers, run water through the instrument for about 10 min.
Shutdown: Same procedure as usual, run “Fluidics Shutdown.”
This should help with any initial issues that you might have. I am available via phone (my cell is if you have any additional questions. Please do not hesitate to reach out if you need anything.
Thanks,
Bryan

Aurora Plate Loader Guide
Cytek Loader Tutorial
Start Up
Make sure that tube is loaded onto Aurora for initial calibration of sample probe.
Remove tube from holder once the initial calibration is completed and the Cytometer is showing ass “Connected.”
Pull lever on loader to the front position.
Turn on loader via the button in the back.
Template Set Up
Go to “Preferences” tab
Under “Sample Delivery Mode” select “Plate”
Check the box for “Bubble/Clog Detection”
Return to “Acquisition” tab.
Click “Add Plate”
Select appropriate type of plate
Label plate accordingly
Click on “Edit” icon
Select “Groups” tab
Select wells that need to be acquired
Can add multiple groups to a plate or make entire plate a single group
Select “Acquisition” tab
Set “Worksheet” to appropriate worksheet you would like to use
Set “Events to Record” to an appropriate value
Set “Storage Gate” to appropriate gate
Set “Stopping Volume” to an appropriate vale
We used 110 µL on Friday.
Select “Loader Settings” tab
Select the appropriate direction for sampling by selecting the arrow icons
Set “Mix Time” to “4”
All other settings should be fine.
Sample Probe Depth Check
Create a new plate with a sample only in well D1
Use an empty plate and fill D1 with water or PBS
Run the sample and look at the probe depth while running
If sample probe appears to touch near the bottom of the plate, you are ready to run samples
If sample probe is too high:
Go to “QC& Setup” side tab
Click on “Calibrate SIT”
Change the value to a smaller number
Run plate again to evaluate new SIT depth setting
Run Plate
Select a well to record data for
Select an appropriate acquisition speed
Click “Record” button and select “Record Well”
If sample settings seem appropriate select “Record Plate” on “Record” button
Shut Down
Move the lever to adjust the loader to the off position (Move lever to the back)
Turn off loader
Under “ Preferences” Tab switch back to “Tube” under “Sample Delivery Method”
Wash with Contrad
Wash with Water
Perform a “Fluidics Shutdown” and turn off Aurora
Troubleshooting/Notes
If plate holder is not in position to load a plate onto it click “Eject” button to return it to the proper position.

title: Cytek Aurora
text: Este es la documentacion para en eltrenamiento para utilizar uno de nuestros Cytek Aurora. Si preferies ver este entrenamiento de forma de un video, por favor procide a YouTube.

title: Cytek Aurora
text:
Rellenando contenedores

Rellenando Sheathe Fluid
Antes de comenzar, recomiendo que cheques los niveles de liquido en los contenedores de “sheathe fluid” y “waste”. El “sheathe fluid” en nuestro “flow core” consiste de agua ultra-pura que fue filtrado por nuestro sistema de MilliQ, que esta ubicada adentra del cuarto de sorteo. Si estas aqui antes o despues de las horas de negocio, puedes encontrar las llaves adentro del primer cajon del escritorio de Mikayla.
Recomemdamos que todo usuario use guantes mientras interactuando con los instrumentos. Aunque toda celula debe estar “fixed”, el uso de contrad y cloro es suficiente que hemos encontrado mejor poner guantes en ves de por accidente quedar en contacto. Ademas, ayuda reducir chance de contaminacion al cuarto de sorteo.



Para el waste, si esta mas de mitad lleno, es recomendado que lo vacies. “EHS” requiere que para disenfectar, an~adimos suficiente cloro para que al nivel final de lleno la contentracion de cloro sea a 10% de todo el volumen del contenedor.
Algo para considerar, es que la botella esta conectada con el “cytometer” por medio de ambo el tubo por cual viaja el “waste”, pero tambien un cable por cual el instrumento puedo verificar el nivel. Porque este cable puedo ser dan~ado si lo “envolvemos”, para remover, recomendamos que agarramos la botella por medio de la capa, y giramos la botella hacia la “derecha?” hasta que se desconecta. Con esto hecho, agarrando con dos
Para el waste, para sanitizar todo, necesitamos anadir cloro para que el volumen final la concentracion quede al 10%. Cuando el tanque/contenedor de waste este lleno, lo que hacemos es agarrramos la capa de la botella, y giramos la botella. Luego al desconectar, ponemos la capa y los tubos de intake en el contenedor temporario.
De ahi, vamos y descartamos con cuidado en el sink. Despues, hacemos un rinse con agua para que no quede nada y para que todos con cual compartimos esto cuarto no estemos oliendo cloro por el resto del dia. Luego, regresamos a lado del LSR-II done guardamos el cloro, y lo rellenamos hasta la line roja, que es lo que necesitamos anadir para el volumen final del 10%. Estos contenedores son un poco mas de 4L, o algo asi. Para el sheathe fluid, no removemos la capa como es el caso con el cloro. La razon es que el waste tiene un sensor electronico, que puede causarnos problemas si lo movemos demasiado, asi que mejor no molestarlo mas de lo que sea necesario.
Para el sheathe, presionamos el boton, que release libera la conexion con los ubos de plastico. De ahi llevamos este al estacion de agua MiliQ, y lo rellenamos ahi.
Si estas aqui durante la semana, normalmente vas a encontrar los instrumentos ya predidos y listos para usar. Eso es porque yo ya estube aqui mas temprano, los prendi, limpie y asegure que pasaron sus chequeos de qualidad, osea, QC. Si llegas depus de horas, o durante el fin de semana, lo que haces es el boton para prender in instrumento esta del lado izquierdo, casi hasta arriva, presiona fuerte para dos segundos para prender el instrumento.
Desde ahi, asegura que la computadora este prendida, usa la contrasena comun para el instrumento cuando Windows pregunte para la contrasena. Cuando todo termine de inicear, lo que vas a brier es el software SpectroFlo, el shortcut atajo que puedes encontrar aqui.
Al iniziar, el software verifica que tienes contrato con Cytek por medio de un SpectroFlo dongle. Por lo menos es el caso con la version 3.2, solo necesitas el dongle puesto en el slot de USB al momento de inicear el software. Si tienes el software instalado en tu laptop/portatil, y quieres analizar n otro lugar por un rato, puedes remover el USB de una maquina que nadie esta utilizando, enchufarlo en tu laptop, entrar tu contrasena, remover el USB y regresarlo al instrumento. Siempre y cuando no te olvides y accidentalmente cierres el programa, vas a poder hacer tu analisis.
En fin, estos SpectroFlo dongles vienen con nuestros instrumentos y queden asi. Asi que siempre estan enchufados con las computadoras de sus respectivas maquinas. Asi que al comenzar el instrumento, podemos procedir directamento entrando la contrasena.
El user se crea por un login del account Admin. La contrasena de Admin es …, si lo se, una contrasena fortisima no creen. De ahi, a ____ y creamos un nuevo usuario. Nombre, contrasena y aqui prolomenos por si acaso se te olvide la contrasena, underscore y el apellido del primer investigador del laboratorio en cual trabajas.
Al regresar a la pagin de login, podemos ver las varias opciones. Para este entrenamiento, voy a concentrar en explicando solo como usar el mode spectral, el modo convencional puede esperar para otro dia.
Desde aqui, despues del login, vemos varias opciones. La mayoria del tiempo para un user, simplemente vamos a estar usando el tab acquision. Vamos a enfocarnos aqui para el momento.
Cuando ya estamos ahi, lo que necesitamos hacer es seleccionar crear un nuevo experimento (en vez de importar un experimento que ya fue previamente creado). Desde aqui, vemos el primer tab, que es donde podemos nombrar nuestro experiment, y seleccionar los fluorophores. Para anadir fluorophores, podemos empezar entrando sus nombres y si ya estan parte del sistema van a aparecer solo los fluorophores que tienen en comun lo que ya teclaste. AL encontrar cual estabas buscando, puedes anadir o hacer un doble clikc para anadirlo. Borra lo que teclaste, y repite el proceso para el resto de tus fluorophore.
Algo que recomiendo yo es que anadelos en order basado en su detector, osea en que lugar el lightspectrum su emisiom maxima ocurre. La razon es que el software va organiza sus controls de referencia basado en este orden que anades los fluorophores en esta pagina, y puede causar dolores de cabeza cuando los organizes de otra manera. Obviamento, preferencia personal, pero cuando estas cansado, descafinado y despelucado aqui despues de horas, vale la pena menos esfuerzo mental de encontrar cual tubo va donde.
En la segunda pagina, tab encontramos donde podemos anadir groupos a nuestro experimento, adentro del cual podemos agregar tubos ubes para specimens individuales. Como organizas tus experimentos va depender de con que estas trabajando, en mi caso, con especimens clinicos, es el numero de identificacion del paciente como grupo, y la condiction en particular del tratamiento como el tubo.
Lo importante es que todos los tubes que anades son specimens, que estan stained con la mescla que contiene todo los fluorophores de tu panel. Para que un experimento de citrometria de flujo spectral funcione, necesitamos tambien proveer otras dos cosas. Tubos conteniendo celulas que no hemos stained con un fluorophore, osea, los unstained. Y que sirven como referencia de autofluorescence. y los controles de referencia individuales para cada uno de tus fluoropjores que tienes en tu panel, o sea, los single-color controls. Como exactamente estos son utilizados, hablaremos mas sobre ellos alrato.
Para el momento, los anadimos encontrando el boton de referencia del group arriva en medio de la pantalla, que tiene un pequeno lapiz como su imagen. Desde aqui, las referencias ya anadidas aparecen para los fluorophores que seleccionaste en la pagina previa. Lo importante de esta pagina es uno, anadir los nombres de los markers asignados, para sus respectivos fluorophores. Despues que entrastes todos, selecciona si tu control de referencia es celulas o beads. Eso informa el sistema cual usar para la subtraccion de autofluorescence. Luego, seleccionas tu preferencia de cual AF quieres usar para la subtraccion. Si lo dejas sin seleccion, anadira ung ate negativo interno en addicional del gate positivo para cada specimen. Esto puede funcionar, pero tambien puedo causar problemas si tienes fluorophores que causan non-specific stains.
Lo opcion normal es que uses un unstained universal, esto te permite dar una referencia de control separado. Esto ayuda esquivar el escenario en cual que el fluorophore anade senal al negativo, que cause que incrementan.
Para anadir otro unstained, seleccionamos esta opcion aqui arriva. Mi practica nornal es nombrar los unstained adicionales basado en que populacion de celulas van a representar si lymphoctyes, , . o celulas muriendo o ya muertas.
Si quieres anadis mas referecias de lo que ya tienes, vas a tener que ir hasta abajo de la pagina a la izquierda, y seleccionar tus opciones. Esto anade un tube de referencia adicional, que puedes cambiar el nomre del fluorophore. Etc como habiamos dicho antes. De aqui procedemos a la pagina que sigue. Esta pagina es donde decimos a SpectroFlo cuantas celulas queremos acquirir. Esto podemos especigicar basado en tubos individuales, al nivel del grupo, o del experimento entero.
La primer columna refiere a cual guate estamos usando par ael crierio de numeros de celulas acquirrido. Yo normalmente quiero acquirir todas las celular, pero si quieres acquirir algo mas especifico, digamos, 5000 celulas cd4, si ya creaste esas puertas, en el tempate, en el drop-down puedes seleccionarlo.
Continuando, puedes decidir si en la version final del fcs file solo quieres tener celular que cayeron adentro de un gate. Esto puede ayudar reducir el tamano de los files. pero al mismo timepo, estas a la merced de que para cada uno de tus especimens aquiridos todas las puertas gates van a estar en la misma posicion, si esto cambia, estas jodido.
